purpose: Data-foundation audit for a rebuild-native nfl-elo-trend-lr candidate. Does NOT fit or evaluate any model; scoped to real backfilled coverage, missingness, PIT status, and servability of the incumbent's exact feature set (elo_probability, trend_gap) from real data only.
commands_run: rebuild-data backfill --sport nfl --season 2021 --table weekly_rosters  (FAILED, see roster_backfill_status)

real_bug_found_and_fixed.symptom: polars.exceptions.ComputeError: could not append value: 66.0 of type: f64 to the builder -- reproduced deterministically backfilling real 2022 schedule data.
real_bug_found_and_fixed.root_cause: pl.DataFrame(rows) defaults to infer_schema_length=100. Nullable columns (temperature_f/wind_mph are None for every dome game; similar for pbp's down/yards_to_go/epa/success on non-play rows, and weekly_rosters' jersey_number/depth_chart_position) can stay None for the first 100+ rows of a real season purely due to row order (e.g. 2022's schedule happens to list >100 dome games before the first outdoor game with a real temperature reading). Polars locks the column to a Null dtype from that 100-row sample, then crashes the instant a real typed value appears later. This is entirely row-order dependent, not a data-content bug -- 2021/2023/2024/2025 schedules happened not to trigger it; 2022 did.
real_bug_found_and_fixed.fix: Pass infer_schema_length=None (scan every row before fixing a dtype) in all three NFL normalizers.
real_bug_found_and_fixed.regression_test: tests/rebuild/test_nfl_data_foundation.py::test_schedule_normalizer_survives_all_null_prefix_longer_than_inference_window -- verified to fail on the pre-fix code (reverted fix, confirmed same ComputeError) and pass after.
real_bug_found_and_fixed.verified_against_real_data: All 5 seasons (2021-2025) schedule backfill succeeds after the fix; 2024 pbp backfill (49,492 real plays) also succeeds.

schedule_coverage.note_2022_count: 284 vs 285 in other seasons is a real nflverse count (one fewer scheduled game record in that release), not a symptom of the schema bug -- confirmed by rerunning post-fix and cross-checking week range/team count are otherwise identical.

pbp_spot_check.note: epa/success are null only on non-play rows (timeouts, two-minute warnings, etc.) -- expected, not a missingness defect.

roster_backfill_status.cli_backfill_result: FAILS for every one of the 5 tested seasons via the wired rebuild-data CLI path
roster_backfill_status.error: ValueError: missing NFL gsis_id, raised from normalize.py::_weekly_rosters -> _required_id
roster_backfill_status.root_condition: A small, real, permanent fraction of weekly roster rows are 'DEV' (practice/development squad) players who have not yet been issued a permanent GSIS ID by the league. The normalizer's identity check is fail-closed by design (never fabricate a player identity) -- this is the same convention used verbatim in the WNBA rebuild normalizer's _player_canonical_id (raises rather than guesses), not a one-off NFL defect.
roster_backfill_status.classification: NOT PATCHED in this pass. This is a real, current, always-reproducible blocker for weekly_rosters specifically, but it is a design decision (how should unidentified practice-squad rows be handled: skip-and-flag vs. hard-fail-the-season) rather than a mechanical bug -- changing it needs an explicit provenance-preserving decision (e.g. a documented synthetic/fallback identity key with its own audit trail), which is out of scope for a data-foundation-only pass per this task's own instructions.
roster_backfill_status.diagnostic_method: Computed directly from the cached NFLVerseProvider raw response (already fetched during the failed backfill attempts), filtering for null/empty gsis_id -- read-only, bypasses the fail-closed normalizer, never written to data/rebuild/normalized. Confirms the blocking condition affects <0.1% of rows every season, i.e. is not a broad data-quality problem, just an edge case the current identity gate does not yet have a policy for.
roster_backfill_status.impact_on_elo_trend_servability: NONE. elo_probability and trend_gap are both derived purely from schedule/game results (features/elo_ratings.py, features/trends.py), never from rosters. Roster data only matters for future QB-identity/injury-state features, which docs/model_audit/features/NFL.md already marks BLOCKED_PIT for a separate, more fundamental reason (see pit_status below).

pit_status.source: NFLFoundation.backfill manifest (foundation.py:97-98), unconditional for every season captured this way
pit_status.reason: nflverse releases are mutable snapshots, not historical observation logs. A season/week label never proves a row was observable at an earlier decision time. This applies uniformly to schedule, pbp, and weekly_rosters -- confirmed unchanged in this pass, not re-derived here (see docs/model_audit/models/NFL_ELO_TREND_LR_V4.md section 6 and docs/model_audit/features/NFL.md).
pit_status.scope_of_blocker: Blocks any walk-forward BACKTEST built on today's bulk download from claiming retrospective PIT validity for EPA/CPOE/pressure/QB-state features specifically. Does NOT block basic Elo/trend feature computation, because Elo/trend only need final game outcomes (home/away score, kickoff time), which are themselves not mutable in any meaningful way after a game completes (score corrections essentially never happen), and because the incumbent nfl-elo-trend-lr-v4's live serving path is PIT-safe by construction (games_before(decision_date) + event-not-started gate) independent of this nflverse pipeline entirely.

basic_elo_trend_servability.verdict: SERVABLE from what is backfilled today, with a caveat
reasoning: elo_probability and trend_gap require only: event_id, event_start_utc, home_team_id, away_team_id, home_score, away_score, completed -- all present, 100% populated, 0 duplicates, 0 timestamp violations across all 5 backfilled seasons (1,424/1,424 games completed).

The rebuild's own build_elo/TrendEngine code (features/elo_ratings.py, features/trends.py) is sport-generic and already exercised in production for the incumbent nfl-elo-trend-lr-v4 -- reusable without modification for a rebuild-native candidate.

The nflverse schedule data is a genuinely independent source from the incumbent's ESPN-sourced data/processed/nfl/games.jsonl (see NFL_ELO_TREND_LR_V4.md section 7), which is the correct posture for an 'independently trained sibling' per docs/model_audit/ARCHITECTURE_CORRECTION.md -- not a copy of the incumbent's training data.
basic_elo_trend_servability.caveat: The retrospective_pit_qualified: false flag is manifest-level and technically applies to schedule too (mutable-release caveat), even though completed-game scores are practically immutable once a game ends. Any future walk-forward validation on this data should still explicitly document this manifest-level caveat rather than silently assuming schedule is exempt -- the audit's recommendation is to note it, not to treat schedule as pre-cleared.

epa_based_feature_status.verdict: BLOCKED_PIT -- unchanged, confirmed, NOT to be worked around
epa_based_feature_status.detail: epa/success are already captured at 98.85% coverage in the pbp normalizer (confirmed via the 2024 spot-check above), but per foundation.py's unconditional retrospective_pit_qualified: False and docs/model_audit/features/NFL.md's epa_per_dropback/success_rate rows, a single bulk download today cannot serve as honest walk-forward backtest evidence for EPA-based features. The documented fix is calendar time (daily observed_at_utc-stamped capture accumulation going forward), not a code or validation change. This audit does not attempt or recommend any workaround.
